topSignals.title: Bloom Energy Q2 transcript published: scandium supply confirmed, BE reverses to ~$160
topSignals.text: — The Q2 earnings call transcript (released July 30) closes the most contested short-seller thesis: CEO KR Sridhar stated Bloom is "not dependent on China" for scandium supply and has visibility for 25 GW of deployments using economically recoverable scandium. Separately, the transcript confirmed the ~$502M Quanta Computer microgrid order (three fully islanded SOFC systems for AI-server manufacturing plants B16/B18/B19 in Fremont, CA). Despite the blowout Q2 beat, BE surged +11% at the July 29 open then retreated sharply, closing approximately -2% at ~$164; the stock has continued lower to ~$160 on July 30 — a profit-taking reversal after the +1,300% run from 2025 lows. Analyst actions: Clear Street upgraded to Buy ($290 PT); UBS revised PT to $300 (from $350). Investing.com transcript | Gurufocus highlights | 24/7 Wall St.

topSignals.title: New York enacts first US statewide data center moratorium — six more states watching
topSignals.text: — Governor Kathy Hochul signed an executive order imposing a one-year ban on state environmental permits for new hyperscale data centers (≥20 MW), the first statewide moratorium of its kind in the US. The legislature passed the Responsible Data Center Development Act on June 4 (Senate 44-16; Assembly 102-39); Hochul signed July 14. Rationale: data centers threaten utility bills, water, and air quality. A Generic Environmental Impact Statement will run during the pause. Minnesota, Michigan, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, New Hampshire, and Virginia are considering similar legislation. SOFC implication: the moratorium targets grid-connected data centers; fully islanded on-site fuel cell generation — SOFC's key differentiator — could become the permitting workaround as the framework develops. CNBC | Stateline | DLA Piper

topSignals.title: Project Jupiter: protestors arrested at July 28 county meeting; Oracle promises 7,000 jobs and fuel-cell confirmation
topSignals.text: — Doña Ana County held its first direct briefing from Oracle/STACK Infrastructure on July 28. Demonstrators were arrested at what the ABQ Journal described as a meeting that "sparks scuffle, arrests." Oracle officials pledged 7,000 jobs (up from the governor's original 1,000 announcement), confirmed the project uses natural gas fuel cells with a 5-7 year lifespan (not gas turbines), and reiterated no public drinking water will be used. Air permit hearing: October 19 unchanged. NM AG criminal investigation into fraudulent public comments ongoing. ABQ Journal – arrests | Searchlight NM | Oracle PR

Bloom Energy Q2 transcript — scandium supply and Quanta microgrid confirmed: See Top Signal #1. Additional transcript datapoint: Fremont factory utilization and shipped MW not yet extracted from full transcript text — monitor Seeking Alpha / Gurufocus for analyst parsing of this figure (key for cost/kW derivation). Project Jupiter — arrests, job promises, fuel-cell lifespan stated: See Top Signal #3. New detail from county meeting: Oracle officials explicitly described the fuel cells as having a "5-7 year lifespan" — this is consistent with SOFC stack replacement economics (Bloom replaces stacks, not entire systems) but may feed opposition narratives about long-term site commitment. The 2.45 GW total commitment remains the largest single SOFC order in history. SemiAnalysis 2029 first-power base case unchanged.

Bloom + Quanta Computer $502M islanded microgrid (Q2 transcript confirmed): Three fully islanded SOFC microgrids for Quanta's AI server manufacturing plants (B16, B18, B19) in Fremont, CA. End-2025 PO, first disclosed in Q2 call context. This is a manufacturing (not data center) use case — significant because it demonstrates SOFC as primary power for 24/7 AI hardware production, not just DC backup. Microgrid Knowledge | Bloom PR
Background (unchanged): 32% of US data centers planning fully off-grid SOFC by 2030. Crusoe/Tallgrass Cheyenne 900 MW Ph.1, FCEL/Fit Energy 380 MW, Equinix 100+ MW — no new updates July 30.

New York 1-year data center moratorium — signed July 14, 2026: See Top Signal #2. Key legal analysis (DLA Piper): the moratorium applies to "state permits" for large-load data centers, not to federal permits or to data centers below 20 MW. On-site islanded generation bypasses the grid-connection trigger that most state energy permitting reviews focus on. If NY becomes a template, the SOFC value proposition in moratorium-affected states becomes structural, not cyclical.

FERC RM26-4: ISO-NE abeyance deadline August 3 (4 days). No new filings or orders found July 30. August 17 hard deadline for all RTOs/ISOs unchanged. Watch for: ISO-NE abeyance grant/denial (shapes PJM/MISO/CAISO/ISO-NE avoided-T-cost modeling window).
State data center legislation wave: PYMNTS notes New York's moratorium "may not be the last" — tracking for Minnesota, Michigan, PA, SC, NH, Virginia developments. PYMNTS

Bulletin of Atomic Scientists: "Don't fall for Big Tech's nuclear PR hype" (July 20, 2026) — Langabeer & Ramana argue that SMRs and next-gen nuclear will be "unable to provide any significant boost to the electricity consumption of data centers anytime soon — especially within the next several years." Key stat: nuclear's global grid share was just 8.8% in 2025, roughly half of 30 years ago. Article directly supports the SOFC near-term competitive advantage narrative: of all on-site power alternatives, only fuel cells and gas engines can deploy on the 90-day timeline AI data centers need. Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists
Background nuclear pipeline unchanged: Microsoft TMI restart (835 MW, 2027), Meta 6.6 GW (2030+), Aalo-X experimental criticality targeted July 2026. No new hyperscaler nuclear signings July 30.

Bloom Energy (BE): ~$160 on July 30, continuing the retreat from the +11% open at $185.85 on July 29 (which gave back gains to close ~$164). The post-Q2 reversal is structurally unusual: revenue $1.065B (+166% YoY), EPS $0.78 (+90% beat), guidance raised to $3.9-4.2B — and yet the stock is now -14% off the post-earnings high and roughly flat vs. the pre-earnings close ($184.89). Likely driver: profit-taking after +1,300% YTD run; market already priced the beat. Analyst upgrades to date: Clear Street Buy $290; UBS revised to $300 (from $350). Wall Street consensus avg. PT: ~$286 (27 analysts). Full upgrade cycle expected over next 48 hrs. 24/7 Wall St. | Yahoo Finance

Ceres Power (LON: CWR): No new news. H1 2026 results (September) next scheduled catalyst. Share price remains ~-40% from June peak.

Advanced Science (Wiley), 2026 — "Catastrophic Degradation in Solid Oxide Fuel Cells Caused by Air Supply Interruption in Real-World Operations: Fundamental Mechanisms and Mitigation Strategies" — Study reveals that air supply interruption to running SOFC stacks causes irreversible chemical degradation of perovskite-based cathode materials. The paper covers mitigation strategies. Directly relevant to real-world SOFC system operations — particularly for data-center deployments where BOP reliability (fans, valves, controls) is a system-level risk rather than a cell material risk. Wiley/Advanced Science

Advanced Science, Vol. 13 (Wiley, 2026) — "Catastrophic Degradation in Solid Oxide Fuel Cells Caused by Air Supply Interruption": See Research & IP above. System-level relevance: air management subsystem reliability is a BOP design constraint for data-center SOFC installations. Mitigation strategies discussed provide design rules for system integrators. LCOE flag: If air supply failure is a credible mode in real operations, stack replacement interval assumptions may need a scenario at 10-12 years rather than 15 years. Wiley
No other new system-level papers identified July 30. Quiet day for LCOE/system TEA research front.

lcoe.text: Scandium supply risk resolved (Q2 transcript): Removes the "China scandium export restriction" bear scenario for capex modeling. The high-case capex scenario driven by rare-earth supply crunch can be retired or substantially reduced in probability weight. Does not change base capex assumption — retain until shipped MW data enables cost/kW derivation.

BE stock pullback ($184.89 → ~$160 in 2 sessions): A 14% post-earnings drop despite a massive beat is a market signal. If institutional investors are rotating out, the implied cost-of-capital for SOFC market participants may be rising, not falling. Monitor BE 5-day VWAP: if it stabilizes above $170, treat as profit-taking; if it continues to $150, raise the LCOE model's discount rate sensitivity by 100-150bp.

New York moratorium — market sizing: If NY triggers copycat legislation in 6 states cited (MN, MI, PA, SC, NH, VA), the addressable market for grid-connected US hyperscale data center builds contracts materially. Counter-effect: moratoriums that exempt islanded/on-site generation shift demand toward SOFC. Net effect on SOFC-specific LCOE model: upward revision to total SOFC demand share of remaining DC market.

Air-supply degradation (Advanced Science 2026): Flag to add "air supply interruption" scenario in lifetime sensitivity: if this failure mode is unmitigated, assume 10-12 year stack life instead of 15 years → increases LCOE by 15-25% in affected scenario. Mitigation strategies in the paper should be reviewed against Bloom's published BOP design.

Pending — Bloom Q2 shipped MW: Still not confirmed from transcript summary. Once extracted: divide Q2 product revenue ($935.4M) by shipped MW to derive implied revenue/kW, then apply gross margin 33.4% to get approximate manufacturing cost/kW. This remains the single highest-priority pending LCOE input.
